lessons.goal: 理解人物目標的改變，依結尾行動推論主旨。

questions.evidence: Before visiting a craft market, Anya promises herself she will buy something special. She walks past stalls of cups, cloth bags, and wooden toys, but nothing fits both her budget and a real use at home. She starts to feel that leaving empty-handed would make the trip a failure.
questions.explanation: 她未找到同時符合預算及實際用途的物品。
options: Nothing fits both her budget and a real use.
The market forbids purchases.
She forgot that she planned to buy something.
Every stall is closed.
questions.prompt: Why doesn't Anya buy from the earlier stalls?

questions.evidence: At the last stall, a maker demonstrates how a flat strip becomes a woven handle. Anya asks several questions and watches closely. The maker lets her practice with spare paper strips, and she takes a photograph of her sample with permission.
questions.explanation: 攤主示範扁條如何編成提把。
options: How to repair a camera.
How to weave a handle from a strip.
How to carve all wooden toys.
How to price every stall.
questions.prompt: What does the maker show her?

questions.evidence: Before visiting a craft market, Anya promises herself she will buy something special. She walks past stalls of cups, cloth bags, and wooden toys, but nothing fits both her budget and a real use at home. She starts to feel that leaving empty-handed would make the trip a failure.
questions.explanation: 她原先以完成購物作為成功標準。
options: She has already learned too many skills.
The maker refuses to speak.
She cannot remember her home.
She defines the trip's success as buying something.
questions.prompt: Why does Anya initially call leaving empty-handed a failure?

questions.evidence: On the way home, Anya realizes she has a new idea to try with paper already in her drawer. She bought no object, yet the visit gave her a skill and a conversation she enjoyed. Her original plan measured success by a purchase. The actual experience offers another measure: something learned that she wants to explore again.
questions.explanation: 末段以購買對比學習收穫。
options: Something bought or the act of buying.
A spare paper strip given for practice.
A photograph taken with permission.
A skill learned through questions.

questions.evidence: On the way home, Anya realizes she has a new idea to try with paper already in her drawer. She bought no object, yet the visit gave her a skill and a conversation she enjoyed. Her original plan measured success by a purchase. The actual experience offers another measure: something learned that she wants to explore again.
questions.explanation: 她獲得技能與想法，可用家中材料再練。
options: She proves all souvenirs are useless.
She secretly takes a market item.
She gains an idea she can practice with existing materials.
She spends more than her budget.
questions.prompt: What makes the visit useful despite no purchase?

options: Every visitor should avoid spending money.
Learning a skill requires owning an expensive object.
A trip is successful only when something is bought.

questions.prompt: Which theme best fits the story?

lessons.story:
Before visiting a craft market, Anya promises herself she will buy something special. She walks past stalls of cups, cloth bags, and wooden toys, but nothing fits both her budget and a real use at home. She starts to feel that leaving empty-handed would make the trip a failure.

At the last stall, a maker demonstrates how a flat strip becomes a woven handle. Anya asks several questions and watches closely. The maker lets her practice with spare paper strips, and she takes a photograph of her sample with permission.

On the way home, Anya realizes she has a new idea to try with paper already in her drawer. She bought no object, yet the visit gave her a skill and a conversation she enjoyed. Her original plan measured success by a purchase. The actual experience offers another measure: something learned that she wants to explore again.
lessons.title: The Return Trip without a Souvenir
